briefBlocks.text: Sprint 3 — Donations Core, Resource Authorization & Production API Engineering

briefBlocks.markdown: In this sprint, you take **DonationHub** — the donation management and crowdfunding platform — from basic CRUD to a **production-ready** platform. You will build the **Donations Core** backed by atomic **EF Core Database Transactions** because any mistake here means an error with real money, enforce **Resource-Based Authorization** ensuring a campaign manager only touches their own campaigns, and add production-grade API features: caching (in-memory then **Redis**), bilingual localization, API versioning, rate limiting, and a strict CORS policy.

- **Duration:** 15 Days (22/11/2026 to 06/12/2026)
- **Stand-up 1 (Day 5):** 26/11/2026 — Session Leader: **Kareem Zein**
- **Stand-up 2 (Day 10):** 01/12/2026 — Session Leader: **Mohamed Atef**
- **Closing & Deadline (Day 15):** 06/12/2026 — Session Leader: **Asma ELhadidy**
- **Code Review & Corrections (Days 16–18):** 07/12/2026 to 09/12/2026
- **Evaluation:** 100 Points

**Target Framework:** .NET 10 (`net10.0`) with the `.slnx` solution format, fully compatible with .NET 8 and .NET 9. We continue on the same solution from Sprint 2: SQL Server + EF Core + **thin Controllers** + MediatR `[12.5.0]`.

Advance DonationHub beyond basic CRUD by implementing the **Donations Core** module backed by atomic **EF Core transactions** to protect financial consistency. Enforce fine-grained **resource-based authorization** (ownership rules), and equip the platform with production-grade API features:

- **Caching:** In-memory first, then distributed cache via **Redis** running inside Docker.
- **Localization:** Bilingual (`ar` / `en`).
- **API Versioning.**
- **Rate Limiting** to prevent abuse.
- Strict **CORS** policies.

Implement ownership rules and access boundaries according to SRS requirement **CMP-07**. The idea: role alone is not enough — being a `CampaignManager` does not mean the user can modify **any** campaign, only their own. This decision can only be made after loading the resource itself, which is why we need **Resource-Based Authorization**.

items: `CampaignManager` can create campaigns, and modify or delete **only their own campaigns**.
`Admin` has full access to manage all campaigns in the system.
Implement `CampaignOwnershipRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement`.
Implement `CampaignOwnershipHandler : AuthorizationHandler<CampaignOwnershipRequirement, Campaign>` and invoke it via `IAuthorizationService`.

**Security Rule:** When an authenticated user attempts to fetch or modify a private resource owned by another user, return **404 Not Found** (`Campaign.NotFound` / `Donation.NotFound`, not 403 Forbidden) to avoid revealing the existence of the resource ID to unauthorized parties.
Unauthenticated requests (without a token) to protected endpoints return **401**.
**Defense in depth (SRS §6.3):** Enforce authorization in the API (policies/roles) **and** check ownership again inside the handler for owned resources (campaigns and donations).
`GET /campaigns/mine` returns the manager's own campaigns **in all statuses** (paged), with both-language fields.

briefBlocks.markdown:
| Endpoint | Campaign Manager | Admin |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /campaigns` | ✅ Creates owned campaign | ✅ Creates campaigns |
| `PUT /campaigns/{id}` | ✅ Own campaigns only | ✅ All campaigns |
| `DELETE /campaigns/{id}` | ✅ Own campaigns only | ✅ All campaigns |
| `GET /campaigns/mine` | ✅ Fetches own campaigns (all statuses) | — |
**404, not 403:** If you return 403 for another manager's campaign, you tell the attacker that this `id` **exists**. The response must be identical to the "Campaign not found" response.

briefBlocks.text: Task 2 — Donations Core & Atomic Database Transactions

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement donation flow requirements from SRS §5.4. Note: this is the first module in the project that deals with **money**, so consistency and concurrency here are not optional optimizations—they are the core of the task.

items: **DON-01:** A logged-in user (Donor, Campaign Manager, or Admin) creates a donation for an active campaign via `POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/donations` with body `{ "amount": 25.00 }`. The donation starts as `Pending`. Return **201 Created** with a `Location` header.

**DON-02:** Reject the donation when the campaign is not `Active` or its `EndDate` has passed (`Campaign.NotActive`, 409), or when the amount is outside the range configured in `DonationOptions` (defaults: min **1.00**, max **10,000.00**) (`Donation.AmountOutOfRange`, 422). These are domain invariants 3 and 4.
**DON-03:** `GET /donations/mine` — the current user lists **their own** donations (paged) with amount, date, status, and campaign title.
**DON-04:** `GET /donations/{id}` — the owner (or Admin) gets one donation by id. Accessing someone else's donation returns **404** `Donation.NotFound` (do not reveal that it exists).
**DON-05:** `GET /admin/donations` (Admin only) — list all donations, paged, with filters: `status`, `campaignId`, `donorId`, and date range (`from`, `to`).

**DON-06 (Temporary stub, Sprints 3–4):** `POST /admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded` (**Admin only**) simulates a successful payment so you can test the full flow before Stripe. A donation that is not `Pending` returns `Donation.InvalidState` (409). **This endpoint is removed in Sprint 5.**

**DON-07 (Success flow in one transaction — SRS §5.5):** Transitioning a donation to succeeded runs inside **one database transaction** (e.g., `await dbContext.Database.BeginTransactionAsync()` or a single `SaveChangesAsync` through the Unit of Work).

**DON-08 (Concurrency-safe `RaisedAmount`):** Two donations succeeding at the same time must **both** be counted. Use the campaign `RowVersion` with a retry on `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`, or an atomic database update (`ExecuteUpdateAsync(... RaisedAmount + amount ...)`). Be ready to explain your choice.

briefBlocks.markdown:
**Success flow steps (DON-07) in order:**

1. Set donation status to `Succeeded`, set `CompletedAt` (from `TimeProvider`), and generate `ReceiptNumber` in the format `DN-{year}-{6-digit sequence}` (e.g., `DN-2026-000042`). The sequence must be **unique even under concurrent success flows** (Database Sequence, or a Unique Index with retry — SRS §9.4).
2. Add the amount to the campaign's `RaisedAmount`.
3. If `RaisedAmount >= GoalAmount`, set the campaign status to `Completed`.
4. Commit. (From Sprint 4, background jobs are enqueued only **after** the commit, never inside the transaction.)

**Late-payment edge case:** If a payment succeeds after the campaign already expired or completed, **accept the money and record the donation as `Succeeded`** (the donor was already charged), and log a warning via `ILogger`. Refunds are BONUS.

**Unit tests (SRS §6.13):** Add unit tests for the new donation invariants (amount range, campaign must be active, final states cannot change, campaign completes when goal is reached) and for the donation handlers (create, get own / 404 for others' donations, mark-succeeded), with the repository and `TimeProvider` faked.

| Method | Path | Access |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/campaigns/{campaignId}/donations` | Donor, Campaign Manager, Admin |
| `GET` | `/donations/mine` | Any authenticated user |
| `GET` | `/donations/{id}` | Owner, Admin |
| `GET` | `/admin/donations` | Admin |
| `POST` | `/admin/donations/{id}/mark-succeeded` | Admin (temporary, removed in Sprint 5) |

briefBlocks.text: Task 4 — Caching: In-Memory First, Then Redis & IDistributedCache (CMP-09)

briefBlocks.markdown: The goal is to understand **why** we move from an in-memory cache to a distributed cache: in-memory caching is fast, but it lives inside a single process, so if you run two instances of the API each instance ends up with different data, and invalidation in one instance does not reach the other. That is why we build **our own abstraction** in Application so switching is just a DI registration change.

items: **Step 1 — In-memory:** Implement the cache-aside pattern using `IMemoryCache` behind your own caching abstraction in the Application layer.
**Step 2 — Distributed:** Switch the implementation to `IDistributedCache` backed by a local **Redis** container (`AddStackExchangeRedisCache`), with durations from `CacheOptions`.
Cache high-frequency public reads (SRS §6.6): categories list.
Cache public campaign list pages and success stories.
Cache campaign details `GET /campaigns/{id}` with sliding and absolute expiration.

**Key naming:** Keys must include the **language** and the **query parameters** (e.g., `campaigns:list:en:page=1:size=20:cat=…:status=…:search=…:sort=…`), otherwise Arabic users will receive English data.

**Cache Invalidation (CMP-09):** Evict related keys immediately when a **campaign** changes (create, update, delete, status change), when a **category** changes, and when a donation succeeds (raised amount changed). Document your invalidation strategy in the README.
**Never** cache user-specific data (e.g., `GET /donations/mine`) under a shared key.

briefBlocks.markdown: Start with Step 1 and test it, then switch to Step 2 by changing **only the service registration** in Infrastructure. If you need to modify any handler when moving to Redis, your abstraction is leaking implementation details.

solutionBlocks.markdown: This is a reference solution illustrating a sound **way of thinking** for each task, not the only approach. It is a direct extension of the Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 solutions: the same entities (`Campaign` and `Donation`), the same `IUnitOfWork` and `IReadDbContext`, the same `Result`, `Error`, and error catalog, and the same MediatR `[12.5.0]`. Focus on the **why** behind each decision — the Explanation question (20 points) will ask "why", not "what".

To keep things concise, not every class is written out in full: similar use cases (such as `DeleteCampaign`, `GetSuccessStories`, and `GetMyDonations`) follow the same pattern shown. Namespace names are approximate — match them to your project. The critical parts (ownership, success flow, concurrency, caching, and the Rate Limiter) are shown in full.

Reminder: `Result`, `Result<T>`, and `Error` are the same ones we defined in Sprint 2 under `DonationHub.Domain.Common` — we do not redefine them here. The following code relies on implicit conversions from `T` and from `Error` to `Result<T>`:

**Why is `[Authorize(Roles = ...)]` not enough?** Because roles are checked **before** loading any data, whereas the question "is this your campaign?" can only be answered after loading the campaign and comparing `CreatedByUserId` with the user's ID. Therefore, we split authorization into two layers (defense in depth):

1. **In the Controller:** A role-based policy (`Admin` or `CampaignManager`) — rejects irrelevant callers early (401/403).
2. **In the Handler:** After loading the campaign, we call `IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(user, campaign, policy)`; if it fails, we return the **same** "not found" error (404).

The handler in Application must not know about `HttpContext`. Therefore, we **extend** `ICurrentUser` from Sprint 2 with `IsAuthenticated` and `IsInRole` (keeping `UserId` as is), and add `ICampaignAuthorizer`. We move `CurrentUser` from `Api/Infrastructure/CurrentUser.cs` to `Api/Authorization` (delete the old file), and move its registration from `Program.cs` to `AddApiAuthorization`:
Now the handler: not found **or** not yours → literally the same response. Also note cache invalidation after saving (Task 4):

`CreateCampaignCommandHandler` takes the owner from `currentUser.UserId` — **never accept `createdByUserId` from the request body**, otherwise any manager could create a campaign under another manager's name. `DeleteCampaignCommandHandler` follows the same pattern of loading, then `CanManageAsync`, then 404.

`GET /campaigns/mine`: filtering by owner happens **inside the query** itself, so other users' campaigns never reach memory at all. The response is in both languages because it is an admin/management endpoint (CMP-11), and it is not cached because it is user-specific:
Use the `{id:guid}` route constraint. Without it, `GET campaigns/mine` could collide with `GET campaigns/{id}` and you would get a 400 because "mine" is not a Guid.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 2 — Donations Core & Atomic Success Flow

solutionBlocks.markdown:
**The most important decision in this sprint: how do we make `RaisedAmount` concurrency-safe?** There are two acceptable options:

| | Optimistic: `RowVersion` + Retry | Atomic Update: `ExecuteUpdateAsync` |
|---|---|---|
| Rules | Stay inside the entity (`MarkSucceeded` → `ApplySucceededDonation`) | Move out to SQL, and the "Completed" rule must be duplicated manually |
| Concurrency | Conflict is detected via `WHERE RowVersion = @original`, then we retry | The database sums directly: `RaisedAmount = RaisedAmount + @amount` |
| Cost | Re-read on conflict (rare) | Bypasses the Change Tracker and Interceptors |

We chose **RowVersion + retry** because `Campaign` already has `RowVersion` (CMP-10), and because it preserves the **Rich Domain Model** we built in Sprint 1: the Domain is what decides when a campaign becomes `Completed`.

First: `DonationOptions` does not depend on anything from Infrastructure, so we move it to `DonationHub.Application/Common/Options/` so the handler can read it (registration stays in Infrastructure as before). An alternative is an abstraction like `IDonationLimits`, but moving the class is simpler and does not break the dependency rule:
**DON-04 — Fetch a single donation:** The "owner or Admin" condition is checked inside the handler (defense in depth), and a non-owner sees the **same** not-found error:

We used the repository intentionally so that testing "404 for another user's donation" is a simple unit test with Moq. Projecting via `IReadDbContext` with `(isAdmin || d.DonorUserId == userId)` inside `Where` is valid and lighter, but testing it requires a database (Integration tests in Sprint 5).

**Receipt number:** We use a **Database Sequence** in SQL Server — the database guarantees that every `NEXT VALUE FOR` returns a distinct number even if a hundred operations request it at the exact same instant, without any locking on our side:

A Sequence does not roll back on rollback, so **gaps** may appear in the numbers — this is acceptable (uniqueness is required, not gapless continuity). And the filtered Unique Index on `ReceiptNumber` from Sprint 1 remains a second safety net.

**Success flow** in a standalone service called by the stub now; in Sprint 5 the webhook applies the same guarantees inside its transaction (and this class is then removed). We add `ClearChangeTracker()` to `IUnitOfWork` (implemented as `db.ChangeTracker.Clear()`) so each retry starts with fresh values:

**Why is a single `SaveChangesAsync` enough?** Because EF Core wraps all commands of a single `SaveChanges` in a transaction automatically: either the donation update and the campaign update are saved together, or nothing is. We only need an **explicit** transaction when we have multiple `SaveChanges` or `ExecuteUpdate` calls that must succeed together.

If you need an explicit transaction (for example, with `ExecuteUpdateAsync`), add it in the UoW with an **Execution Strategy**, because `EnableRetryOnFailure` rejects user-initiated transactions outside of it:

**Soft-deleted campaign with a Pending donation:** The Global Query Filter hides it, so `GetByIdAsync` returns `null`. Decide on your policy and document it: either forbid deleting a campaign that has `Pending` donations, or load it with `IgnoreQueryFilters()` in the success flow because the money has actually arrived.
**Unit tests — Domain invariants:** Very easy because time is passed as a `DateTime utcNow` parameter:
**Handler tests:** The repository is mocked with Moq, and time is faked with `FakeTimeProvider` (`Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing` package):

Testing "two concurrent donations are both counted" cannot be written as a true unit test because the conflict happens in the database. You can test the retry logic by making `SaveChangesAsync` throw `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` on the first call only (`SetupSequence`), while the real test belongs in Integration tests in Sprint 5.

**The idea:** All filters, sorting, and `Skip`/`Take` are built on `IQueryable` so they translate into a single SQL query, and nothing executes until `CountAsync` and `ToListAsync`. If `ToList()` appears before `Skip`, you are loading the entire table into memory — which is an explicit check in the Definition of Done.

`ThenBy(c => c.Id)` is not cosmetic: if you sort by `EndDate` and ten campaigns share the same date, SQL Server is not required to preserve a deterministic order among them, so a campaign might appear on both page 1 and page 2. And `success-stories` is almost the same handler with `Status = Completed`.
Admin list (DON-05) — filters are optional and are added to the `IQueryable` only when provided. We add `Donations` to `IReadDbContext`, and use `join` because `Donation` has no navigation property:

`GetMyDonationsQuery` (DON-03) is the same query with a fixed condition `d.DonorUserId == currentUser.UserId` and the campaign title in the request language — **and is never cached** under a shared key. The `(DonorUserId, CreatedAt)` index from Sprint 1 serves this query directly.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 4 — Caching: From IMemoryCache to Redis

solutionBlocks.markdown:
**Why our own abstraction?** If you used `IMemoryCache` directly in the handlers, moving to Redis would mean modifying every handler. With a small abstraction in Application, switching from Step 1 to Step 2 is **one registration line** in Infrastructure — and that is what you must be able to demonstrate in review.

**Invalidation strategy:** `IDistributedCache` does not support "delete all keys starting with…". Therefore:
- **Campaign details and categories:** known keys → we delete them directly (for each language).
- **List pages:** unbounded in number (every filter combination), so we embed a **version number** (`v{version}`) stored in a separate key inside the list cache key. Invalidation = changing the version number, so all old pages become unreferenced and expire on their own.
**Step 2 — Distributed via Redis:** The same interface, but values are serialized to JSON because Redis stores bytes rather than .NET objects:
Campaign details with sliding and absolute expiration. Notice that `progressPercent` and `daysLeft` are computed **after** reading from the cache because `daysLeft` depends on the current time:

**The most dangerous caching bug:** Forgetting the language in the key, or caching `GET /donations/mine` under a key without the user ID. The first shows English data to an Arabic user, and the second **leaks one user's donations to another user**. Simplest rule: user-specific data stays out of the cache in this sprint.

**Invalidation everywhere data changes:** `Create/Update/DeleteCampaign` → `InvalidateCampaignAsync`, `Create/Update/DeleteCategory` → `InvalidateCategoriesAsync`, and `DonationSuccessFlow` → `InvalidateCampaignAsync`. Document this in the README:

solutionBlocks.code:
## Caching (Sprint 3)

| Data | Key | Expiration | Invalidated when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Categories list | `categories:list:{lang}` | 60 min absolute | category created / updated / deleted |
| Campaign list pages + success stories | `campaigns:list:v{version}:{lang}:{query}` | 2 min absolute | `campaigns:list:version` gets a new value |
| Campaign details | `campaigns:details:{id}:{lang}` | 5 min sliding, 30 min absolute | that campaign changes, or one of its donations succeeds |

Strategy: details keys are removed directly (both languages). List pages cannot be
enumerated in Redis, so every list key contains a version stamp; changing a campaign,
a category, or a successful donation writes a new version, which makes all old pages
unreachable (they expire on their own). User-specific data (`/donations/mine`) is never cached.

Try it:

    docker run -d --name redis -p 6379:6379 redis:alpine
    dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Redis" "localhost:6379" --project src/DonationHub.Api
    docker exec -it redis redis-cli KEYS "donationhub:*"

solutionBlocks.markdown:
**Decision:** We localize in **three places only**, each with a clear mechanism:

1. **Validation messages:** Built-in FluentValidation messages are localized automatically according to `CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture` (the library ships with Arabic translations), and custom messages use `IStringLocalizer<ValidationMessages>`.
2. **Error messages:** The error catalog remains `static` with fallback English text, and we translate at the **API boundary** by looking up `error.Code` in `ErrorMessages.resx`. That way no handler needs to know anything about language.
3. **Public fields:** Projection selects `TitleAr` or `TitleEn` based on the request language.

Resource files live in `DonationHub.Application/Resources/` (`ErrorMessages.resx` + `ErrorMessages.ar.resx`, and `ValidationMessages.resx` + `ValidationMessages.ar.resx`), along with empty marker classes with the same names in the `DonationHub.Application.Resources` namespace: `public sealed class ErrorMessages { }` and `public sealed class ValidationMessages { }`. The key is the error code itself:

solutionBlocks.markdown: **The `ResourcesPath` trap:** If you write `AddLocalization(o => o.ResourcesPath = "Resources")` while the marker class already lives in the `DonationHub.Application.Resources` namespace, the localizer will look for `DonationHub.Application.Resources.Resources.ErrorMessages` and find nothing — and the keys themselves will be returned instead of the strings **with no error thrown**. Rule: either `ResourcesPath` or a marker inside the Resources folder, never both.

**Evolving `ApiControllerBase` from Sprint 2 (same file, no new helper):** `ProblemFrom(Error)` remains the single place that converts errors to ProblemDetails, and we add two things to it: (1) localizing `title` by looking up `error.Code` in `ErrorMessages.resx` with fallback to the English text from the catalog, and (2) the two methods `FromResult(Result)` → 204 and `FromResult<T>(Result<T>)` → 200 so controller actions become one-liners. Sprint 2 behavior stays intact: `ToStatusCode()` (including 413), the `code` field, `traceId`, and `errors` for validation failures. And on 201 success we use `CreatedAtAction(...)`, and `ProblemFrom` on failure:

**Versioning:** What matters here is that the **ApiExplorer group name** (`v1`) matches the **OpenAPI document name** (`v1`), because built-in OpenAPI places into each document the endpoints whose `GroupName` equals the document name:

**Migrate Sprint 1–2 controllers** (`Auth`, `AdminStaff`, `Categories`, `Campaigns`) to `[ApiVersion("1.0")]` and `api/v{version:apiVersion}/...` instead of `api/v1/...`. **Verify:** open `/openapi/v1.json` and confirm all endpoints appear with `/api/v1/...` paths. The `AddDocument` signature varies slightly across versions of `Scalar.AspNetCore` — check the linked codewithmukesh article.

**Rate Limiting:** Three design points:
- **Partition key:** `global` and `auth` by IP; `donations` by **user** (otherwise users behind the same NAT consume each other's quota).
- **Limits from `RateLimitOptions`** read from `RequestServices` inside the partitioner, so they remain configurable without code changes.
- **Rejection** returns 429 + `Retry-After` + ProblemDetails with the same shape as all other errors.

**Middleware order matters:** `UseRateLimiter()` must come **after** `UseAuthentication()`, otherwise `http.User` will be empty and the `donations` policy degrades to "per IP". `UseRequestLocalization()` comes before it so the 429 message is localized. Apply the policies with attributes: `[EnableRateLimiting(RateLimitPolicies.Auth)]` on `register`, `login`, and `refresh` in `AuthController`, `[EnableRateLimiting(RateLimitPolicies.Donations)]` on donation creation, and `[DisableRateLimiting]` on the webhook in Sprint 5 (bypasses both the global and named policies).

**Why explicit origins?** `AllowAnyOrigin()` means any website on the internet can call the API from a user's browser. And with `AllowCredentials()`, ASP.NET Core rejects that combination outright because it would allow any site to send the user's cookies. We use Bearer tokens in the `Authorization` header, so we **do not need** `AllowCredentials` at all.

`Access-Control-Expose-Headers` is necessary for `Location` and `Retry-After`: without it, browser JavaScript cannot read these headers even when present in the response. Watch out: an origin with a trailing slash (`http://localhost:5173/`) will never match — which is why we validate it at startup.

items: Returning **403** when requesting another manager's campaign or another user's donation instead of **404** — reveals that the resource exists.
Checking ownership only in the Controller (or only in the handler) instead of both layers together (defense in depth).
Accepting `createdByUserId` or `donorUserId` from the request body instead of taking it from the token via `ICurrentUser`.
Modifying `RaisedAmount` via `campaign.RaisedAmount += amount` from outside the entity, or saving the donation and campaign in two separate `SaveChanges` calls without a transaction.
Not handling `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` — causing one of two concurrent donations to be lost or the user to receive a 500.
Generating `ReceiptNumber` with `MAX(...) + 1` or an in-memory counter — produces duplicates under concurrency or after a restart.
Rejecting a late payment on an expired campaign instead of accepting it and logging a warning (the donor was already charged).
`ToList()` before `Skip/Take`, or `CountAsync` after `Skip`, which returns the page count instead of the total count.
Dynamic sorting directly from a user-supplied column name (Reflection or string-interpolated SQL) instead of a whitelist.
A cache key without the language or without all query parameters, or caching `/donations/mine` under a shared key.
Forgetting to invalidate the cache after a successful donation, leaving the old raised amount visible in lists and details.
Hard-coded Arabic strings inside handlers instead of `.resx` files, or auto-translating stored data.
`UseRateLimiter()` before `UseAuthentication()`, causing the `donations` policy to become per IP instead of per user.
429 without a `Retry-After` header or with a plain-text body instead of ProblemDetails with `code: Common.RateLimited`.
`AllowAnyOrigin()` in CORS, or hard-coded origins in code instead of `CorsOptions`.
A Redis or SQL Server connection string written in `appsettings.json` and pushed to Git.

solutionBlocks.text: Questions to Prepare For in Review

items: How did you make `RaisedAmount` concurrency-safe? Why did you choose `RowVersion` + retry instead of `ExecuteUpdateAsync` (or vice versa)? What happens on the third failed attempt?
Why is a single `SaveChangesAsync` enough to act as a transaction? When do you need an explicit `BeginTransactionAsync`, and why with an Execution Strategy?
How do you guarantee `ReceiptNumber` uniqueness under concurrent success flows? Are gaps in the sequence a problem?
Why 404 and not 403 for another user's resource? What is the difference between 401, 403, and 404 in your project?
Why is `[Authorize(Roles = "CampaignManager")]` not enough to protect `PUT /campaigns/{id}`?
Why must the language be included in the cache key? Explain the invalidation strategy for list pages with `IDistributedCache`.
What happens to the API if the Redis container stops? And what happens with in-memory caching if you run two instances of the API?
Why do we localize error messages at the API boundary rather than inside the handlers?
Why is the `donations` policy partitioned per user while `auth` is per IP?
Why is CORS not server protection? And why do we not need `AllowCredentials` with Bearer tokens?

solutionBlocks.markdown: **DON-11 (Anonymous donation):** Add `bool IsAnonymous` to `Donation.Create` and to the request. Hiding happens in the **public projection** only (`DonorName = d.IsAnonymous ? null : u.FullName`) — Admin and the owner see everything.

**DON-12 (Recent donors):** `GET /campaigns/{id}/recent-donors` reads `Succeeded` donations only, ordered by `CompletedAt` descending, with `Take(10)`. It can be cached since it is public (the key includes the campaign), and invalidated inside `InvalidateCampaignAsync`.

**CMP-12 (Cancelled):** Add the value to `CampaignStatus` and include it in `IsFinal`, plus a `Cancel(DateTime utcNow)` method invoked after `CanManageAsync`. Decide what happens to `Pending` donations — and document the decision.
**CMP-13 (Specification):** Encapsulate the filters in a single testable class instead of a chain of `if` statements inside the handler:

**API v2 of one endpoint:** Add `"v2"` to `ApiDocuments.All`, and create a separate controller with `[ApiVersion("2.0")]` on the same route. The `/openapi/v2.json` document will appear automatically because `GroupNameFormat` generates `v2`. A good example: v2 of `GET /campaigns` returns `progressPercent` inside each item — a response-shape change that does not break v1 clients.

If your solution upholds the same **principles** — two-layer ownership checks with 404, a concurrency-safe success flow in one transaction, a database-guaranteed unique receipt number, SQL-level pagination, caching with language-aware keys and documented invalidation, localization via `.resx`, and config-driven rate limiting and CORS policies — it is a valid solution even if names and details differ.
